clue.text: Indicate that the game must stop and report bad goings-on

definitions.text: Indicate that the game must stop
definitions.meaning: a referee signals a halt in play by sounding a whistle
a whistleblower exposes wrongdoing inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A referee halts play, and someone exposes wrongdoing: two scenes run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a referee stopping play and idiomatically means exposing wrongdoing to the authorities.

clue.text: Location near Heathrow reported evidence of pollution

indicators.note: reported means the place name is to be taken as spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Staines is a town in Surrey just south-west of Heathrow airport

explanation.surface: A news item about dirt found near the London airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a Thames-side town beside Heathrow, London's main airport; said out loud it matches the plural of a mark or blot.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks and discolourations left by contaminants are visible signs that something has been polluted.

clue.text: Rapidity with which star dismisses bishop

indicators.note: dismisses means the star sends one letter away, removing it

parts.note: a star is a famous person, a celebrity
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A celebrity quickly sacks a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal synonym for speed or swiftness of movement.

clue.text: Comprehend what thief in art gallery wants to do?

definitions.meaning: to understand, informally to grasp the situation

definitions.text: what thief in art gallery wants to do?
definitions.meaning: an art thief literally wants to acquire a painting

explanation.surface: Understanding what an art thief is after.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to understand a situation; read literally it is to obtain a painting.

clue.text: Daughter and son full of wickedness — real baddies

indicators.note: full of means the two children enclose the next word's letters

parts.note: evil is a synonym for wickedness

explanation.surface: Two children so wicked they are true villains.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiends and demons are the archetypal villains, so they are baddies in the fullest sense.

clue.text: Frenzy to squash maggot turning up in Canadian location

indicators.note: to squash means the frenzy closes round and presses in the following letters

parts.note: mania is a frenzy of excitement

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word for maggot is read bottom to top

parts.note: a bot is the maggot of the botfly

explanation.surface: Someone frantically crushing a grub found somewhere in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of Canada's prairie provinces.

clue.text: Literary communication sent to editor

parts.note: a letter is a written communication

explanation.surface: A letter posted to a newspaper editor about books.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lettered is well read and educated, versed in literature.

clue.text: Settled up with material help

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
aid is a synonym for help

explanation.surface: Someone cleared a debt with practical assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material help' reads as one phrase, but material is the fabric rep.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle up is to pay back what is owed, the past tense matching.

clue.text: Find a cry gone, OK? Possibly, when justice finally triumphs

indicators.note: possibly means the letters given may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about finding a lost cry, ending on judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the time when wrongs are finally punished, originally the Last Judgment.

clue.text: Hero engages us, troubled by this threat to the environment

indicators.note: troubled means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A hero recruits us, worried by an environmental menace.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide and similar emissions trap heat in the atmosphere and drive global warming.

clue.text: Completely blameless person in indoor game

definitions.meaning: in chess one player has the pale pieces and is named for them

explanation.surface: An innocent player at a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour stands for purity and innocence, and names the chess player who moves first.

clue.text: Great heat with dirty riot turning nasty

indicators.note: turning nasty means the riot goes wrong, its letters scrambled

explanation.surface: A sweltering day as a dirty riot turns ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid means scorching hot, and the noun form describes intense heat.

clue.text: Lodging in house with something that adds interest

parts.note: spice is something that adds zest or interest

explanation.surface: Lodgings in a house that has a little extra appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a hospice was a guest-house for travellers, especially one kept by monks.

clue.text: Only some cease offending and become less intense

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice that a few people stop misbehaving and calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'and' in the definition; it only joins the wordplay to the definition, and the definition is the verb phrase alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen in force or slacken is a phrasal-verb synonym for diminishing.

clue.text: Who so hated dying, undone by poison?

indicators.note: undone means the words are taken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Asking who, though loathing death, was killed by poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Bittersweet, a toxic climbing plant of the potato family, has poisonous berries.

clue.text: Manages to be abroad, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken as spoken, giving another of the same sound

parts.note: overseas means abroad, in a foreign country

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to be out of the country, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct is to manage, both in the third person singular.

clue.text: Newspaper in expression of grief over everyone in game

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first part sits above the next
in means the newspaper goes inside the expression of grief

parts.note: a sob is an expression of grief
FT is the Financial Times
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lament over everyone involved in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a team sport like baseball played with a larger ball, an example of a game.

clue.text: Imprecise during performance, no longer retained

indicators.note: retained means the former two pieces hold the next one inside them

parts.note: in means during
an act is a performance
ex means former, no longer

explanation.surface: A sloppy performer no longer kept on.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact is a direct synonym for imprecise, lacking accuracy.

clue.text: A broadcast about two females in naughty relationship?

indicators.note: about means the first two pieces go round the next one

parts.note: to air is to broadcast
F is the abbreviation for female, so two give FF

explanation.surface: A programme about two women in a scandalous liaison.
explanation.definitionFit: An extramarital romance or liaison is the naughty kind of relationship meant.

clue.text: Take vestments off — fantastic fun — groove to the music!

indicators.note: fantastic means the word fun is wildly rearranged

parts.note: to rock is to move rhythmically to music

explanation.surface: Throw off your robes and dance: a cleric's wild night.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrocking a priest literally removes the clerical frock, stripping holy orders.

clue.text: Old jail with priest brought out for prayer

indicators.note: brought out means the priest is removed from the jail

parts.note: prison is a jail

explanation.surface: A priest released from an old jail, leading to prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orison is an archaic, literary word for a spoken prayer.

clue.text: Assignment for church to form working party

parts.note: a task is an assignment
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church job leads to a committee being set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A group formed to tackle a specific problem is a working party.

clue.text: Child, one imprisoned in outbuilding

indicators.note: imprisoned in means the numeral is locked inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a barn is a farm outbuilding
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A child locked in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scots dialect term for a child.

clue.text: Man possibly avoiding awful mincemeat — it can make you sick

indicators.note: awful means the letters of the mincemeat are mangled
avoiding means the letters of the man's name are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A man steering clear of dreadful mince pie filling that may cause vomiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M, A and N from MINCEMEAT and rearrange the rest; 'possibly' flags that MAN is to be found scattered, not in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Lad with no win — awful fix

indicators.note: awful means the letters are in a dreadful jumble

explanation.surface: A boy who never wins is stuck in a terrible jam.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something firmly or settle it definitively is to fix it.
